summary.headline: Zee Q4 FY26: digital revenue up 71% YoY to INR4,700 mn and ZEE5 EBITDA positive for FY26, but ad revenue fell 4% on a March West Asia hit and a INR4,084 mn one-off charge.
summary.overview: Management reported that ZEE5 revenue grew 71% YoY to INR4,700 million in Q4 FY26, its highest ever, and that digital delivered positive EBITDA for FY26 versus a loss of INR5,480 million a year earlier. Linear advertising revenue declined 4% YoY as advertisers pulled spends in March amid the Middle East conflict; management said it would have been low single-digit growth excluding March. A one-off charge of INR4,084 million from a change in movie rights amortization (front-loaded to 50% over two years) and additional impairment was taken in the quarter, and the adjusted EBITDA margin was 6.9% on a 7% decline in operating revenue. Management gave no formal guidance, and the call was mainly Q&A on Zee Music, Bullet, live events, ad spend and manpower costs.

segments.name: Digital (ZEE5)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 71% YoY in Q4 to INR4,700 million, the highest ever for the segment; more than 120 shows and movies released including 34 originals across 7 languages. Management said it is operationally profitable and expects momentum to continue in the medium term.

segments.name: Broadcast / Linear TV
segments.commentary: Advertising revenue fell 4% YoY in Q4 as March spends were held back; Zee TV GRPs grew 40% and the Hindi GEC claims prime-time leadership. Network share 17.4% in Q4, above 18% exiting March.

segments.name: Music
segments.commentary: Over 217 billion total video views and more than 176 million YouTube subscribers in FY26 from a catalogue of over 20,000 songs; management called profitability healthy but gave no revenue disclosure.

segments.name: Studios
segments.commentary: Released 13 movies in Q4 (9 own productions, 4 distribution deals); syndication was strong but Studio sales and services fell 47% YoY in Q4.

segments.name: New initiatives (Bullet, CORE, Phantom)
segments.commentary: Board approved INR20 crore investment in CORE Pvt Ltd (live events) and up to INR116 crore in listed VFX firm Phantom Digital Effects Ltd. Bullet micro-drama app is growing but its potential is still being evaluated.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 guidance; CEO said he cannot guarantee a return to high-teens margins.
Management aims to bring people cost back toward about 9% of revenue, the pre-pandemic level.
Ad environment expected to stay challenging in the near term while the West Asia crisis continues; medium-term view positive.
ZEE5 aspiration is an ad-to-subscription revenue mix of about 50:50 in the medium term.
Digital investment is at optimum level; any increase will not move the EBITDA needle materially, per CEO.
capex_capacity: Content inventory, advances and deposits reduced to INR67.6 billion (down INR2.8 billion YoY) as fresh acquisitions were optimized.
Movie amortization changed from straight-line over 5 years to 50% in the first 2 years and the balance over the next 3 years; total tenure unchanged.
INR20 crore investment approved in CORE Pvt Ltd for live events; up to INR116 crore approved in Phantom Digital Effects Ltd for VFX, animation, gaming and comics.
Bullet micro-drama app investment of about INR100 crore planned over the next few years, per analyst question.
demand_pricing: Advertising: healthy in January and February, but March was severely hit by the Middle East conflict; advertisers are cautious.
Network share rose 80 bps YoY to 17.4% in Q4; management says the 13-16 week lag before viewership gains convert to ad revenue is the reason for the gap.
Zee TV GRPs up 40%; the channel was ahead of its nearest competitors for 26 straight weeks, per management.
ZEE5 growth driven by telco pricing catch-up, B2B activity and the syndication vertical; management does not disclose DAU/MAU or subscriber numbers.
Monthly unique reach across platforms above 800 million; weekly reach above 740 million on linear TV.

qa_highlights.question: Why invest in VFX (Phantom) and how large is the investment and revenue impact? Will FY27 be a content reinvestment year for ZEE5?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said VFX is complementary to the business and will come to television, so in-house is seen as more cost-effective. He said ZEE5 investment is at an optimum level and will not materially move EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Would Zee consider unlocking value in Zee Music?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the focus is expanding the catalogue, and that a demerger with a strategic partner is open to consideration if the offer is right. Metric disclosure is delayed for competitive reasons; disclosure to start sooner or later.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the ad spend line rise 44% in Q4 when FMCG budgets are being cut?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said marketing is needed for new launches and daily consumption businesses cannot pull back. Focus is on making marketing more efficient rather than cutting it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs fall 16% in Q4 and 9% for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to manpower rationalization over the past year through the omnichannel strategy, with roles reassigned and KPIs expanded. The CEO said this is not a one-quarter event.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised movie amortization policy and what is ZEE5 EBITDA excluding the change?
qa_highlights.answer: Amortization is now 50% in the first two years and the balance over the next three. ZEE5 EBITDA excluding the adjustment is below INR100 million for Q4, though shared inventory makes this hard to split.

qa_highlights.question: Why did viewership share fall sequentially from 17.8% to 17.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO cited the T20 World Cup, Bengal elections and other events; said the YoY improvement is still significant and granular data is needed.

risks_watch: Ad revenue: March weakness from West Asia may persist; watch whether Q1 FY27 ad revenue returns to growth.
Margins: FY26 adjusted margin was 8-9% and management gave no path to high teens; watch the ad spend and people cost trend.
Amortization change: the front-loaded policy will weigh on reported profit in FY27 and should be tracked against the one-off charge.
Viewership-to-revenue conversion: a 13-16 week lag is expected, so Q1 FY27 ad revenue should show the network share gain if conversion works.
Zee Music and Bullet: no metric disclosure yet; a demerger or strategic partner for Zee Music is possible but not confirmed.
Receivables: a provision of about INR70 crore for doubtful debts was made at year-end and the company says it is collectible.
summary.management_tone: Confident on digital and long-term strategy, but cautious on the near-term ad market, which management attributes to the West Asia conflict. Evasive on FY27 margin targets and on the viewership-to-revenue gap; it avoided quantifying ZEE5 metrics and Zee Music disclosures.
key_quotes: The platform was operationally profitable for the second quarter in a row, delivering 53% year -on-year growth in FY26.
So, whether we get to the high teens or this thing number, I can't guarantee right now because I can't give you a guidance.
We cannot pull back on marketing from that perspective.
As we look ahead, with the ongoing West Asia uncertainty, we noticed advertisers are adopting a cautious approach.

growth.why: No numeric FY27 guidance; management withdrew the high-teens margin aspiration ("I can't give you a guidance") and said the ad environment stays challenging near term, with no capacity additions or orders to back growth. Q4 operating revenue fell 7% YoY, with ZEE5 up 71% offset by ad revenue down 4%.
